address: Grasweg 41S, Amsterdam-Noord (Buiksloterham): 2010 silver metal-panel industrial block 36 m high with a dark cap edge and sparse small windows, a white pitched hall to the west
notes: Feedback 7f82ac01 (2026-10-28, 'this grey building looks wrong'): panoramas 2024-10-21 (from 209 deg, 174 m), 2021-01-22 (from the IJ, 270 deg) and 2025-06-30 (from 88 deg) show light silver metal cassette cladding (white in sun, cyan-grey overcast; sampled #b5d8e7 cast, #fefefe sunlit, #4c6b84 in shade), a thin dark cap edge, rows of small square windows on the south, west and east faces, and the 45-degree hall to the west in white. The old recipe drew the whole block mid grey with one windowed wall, which read as a dark featureless slab in game. Now: panels cladding at 1.5 m on every face of the tall block, cornice cap, sparse window rows on S/W/E per photo, white pitched roofs. Windows are an even grid of 4 per row on the rows the photos show; the real ones are scattered unevenly (the kit has no irregular window scatter).

Grasweg 41S (BAG, 2010; Buiksloterham, Noord): a 36 m grey metal-clad industrial block with a curved eaves line and low annexes (6.9-8.9 m) to the west. The panoramas show it only through tree cover and over a blue site fence: w01-349 (north, 22 m away) is all foliage, w05-80 (east, 34 m, 20 degree obliquity) shows the grey cladding with a few small windows under a curved cap, w08-349 shows the low annex behind the fence.

walls[0] = panel 45 (E, 24.6 m, party 6.9 m below): the grey cladding with small windows in three rows, drawn as 9 storeys x 4 bays of low windows with the other storeys blank (render/stone material grey). Every other wall is blank grey (palette brick set to the cladding grey) and the flat roof is bitumen. Simplified: the curved cap on the eaves line (straight in 3DBAG), the horizontal cladding ribs, the window positions (read from one oblique photo).
Not drawn or not seen: the north, south and west walls (tree cover) and the annexes.
